content:
A 51-year-old man in Jackson, Mississippi was arrested last Friday in connection with the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black mother who was found hanging from a tree on August 3.

The Jackson Police Department identified the suspect as Jacques Ratliff at a press conference last Friday, and announced his arrest.

Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney said there is some kind of "connection" between the two, but did not specify the nature of their relationship. She also indicated that at least one more arrest warrant may be issued.

Brackney said police executed two search warrants last Friday. The suspect was not at the scene at the time of the incident, but was later arrested on Capitol Street.

Brackney said the arrest came after the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's Office ruled Fortune's death a homicide, and following an extensive investigation and more than a dozen interviews.

"Today's arrest is a significant development in the investigation, but it is not the end," Brackney said. She also urged the public not to speculate about Fortune's death, adding: "We owe it to Ms. Fortune, to her family, and to the integrity of this investigation to let the evidence lead the way."

Fortune's aunt, Etta Avolio, described her in a GoFundMe campaign as "a determined, kind-hearted, and vibrant young woman" and a mother of four children.

Avolio added: "The family also wants the outside world to know that justice will eventually be served. They are holding onto their faith, believing that in the midst of this grief, God is with them."

Fortune's death has drawn comparisons to a similar case — that of Trey Reed, a 21-year-old Black student who was found hanging on the campus of Delta State University in Mississippi in September 2025.

The Mississippi State Medical Examiner's Office ruled his death a suicide, but his family has been seeking an independent autopsy. In July this year, the family said civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who had been working with them on the case, had not been in touch for months and had never provided the results of an independent autopsy.

On the same day as Reed, a 35-year-old homeless white man, Cory Zukatis, was also found hanging from a tree in Vicksburg, Mississippi. Authorities said the case was unrelated to Reed's, and his death was also ruled a suicide.

The case of 18-year-old Nolan Xavier Wells has also drawn attention recently. His friend returned home alone after a boat outing on July 4, despite the fact that Wells had joined them on a trip to Horn Island, eight miles off the Mississippi coast. Wells' parents have called for "honesty and transparency" from all parties involved.
